summary.headline: Carborundum Universal Q1 FY27 standalone sales rose 21.2% YoY to INR 846 crores; consolidated PAT up 23.4% to INR 76 crores, with Electrominerals up 33%.
summary.overview: Standalone sales grew 21.2% YoY to INR 846 crores, broad-based across Electrominerals (+33%), Ceramics (+15.2%) and Abrasives (+14.7%), and were flat QoQ. Standalone PAT was INR 88 crores, up 14.3% on a like-to-like basis excluding a one-time INR 68 crore subsidiary dividend in Q1 FY26. Consolidated PAT of INR 76 crores was helped by a INR 25 crore gain on leasehold transfer at Sterling Abrasives, while Abrasives standalone margins were squeezed by an oil-linked and fuel cost push of about INR 16 crores. Management raised the consolidated Ceramics growth guidance to 23-25% and kept other segment guidance unchanged, while Foskor divestment and Awuko closure updates are now promised for Q2.

segments.name: Electrominerals (standalone)
segments.commentary: Sales INR 282 crores, +33% YoY and +12.2% QoQ, mainly volume and export-led with very little price increase; PBIT rose to INR 39 crores from INR 7 crores. Exports rose to about 40% of segment sales from about 35% last year.

segments.name: Ceramics (standalone)
segments.commentary: Sales INR 274 crores, +15.2% YoY but -1.6% QoQ on refractories seasonality; PBIT INR 59 crores vs INR 62 crores YoY as IC gains were offset by fuel, alumina and unabsorbed costs in new semicon and aerospace/defence lines.

segments.name: Abrasives (standalone)
segments.commentary: Sales INR 328 crores, +14.7% YoY, volume-driven; PBIT INR 34 crores with margin falling to 10.4% from 13.1% YoY, due to about INR 16 crores cost push (resins, oil, fuel) and INR 8-9 crores volume drop QoQ.

segments.name: Rhodius (Germany, Abrasives)
segments.commentary: Sales EUR 15.6 million, +18% YoY and +1.1% QoQ (INR 172 crores, +33.9% YoY); loss after tax EUR 0.7 million vs EUR 1.6 million a year ago. FY27 guidance of about 5% growth and a small PAT loss is maintained.

segments.name: CUMI Awuko Abrasives (Germany, being wound up)
segments.commentary: Sales EUR 2.89 million, +11.1% YoY; loss after tax EUR 1.69 million vs EUR 0.9 million a year ago. Voluntary winding up is in progress and management aims to complete it in about a quarter.

segments.name: VAW Russia (Electrominerals)
segments.commentary: Sales RUB 1.58 billion, -14.1% YoY in roubles but INR 201 crores, +3.1% YoY in rupee terms; PAT RUB 52.1 million vs RUB 71.5 million a year ago. Business is domestic-focused.

segments.name: Foskor Zirconia (51% subsidiary, Electrominerals)
segments.commentary: Sales ZAR 107 million, -14.7% QoQ; deemed commercially unviable. Q1 consolidated PBIT absorbed a INR 17 crore loss; divestment or exit options are being explored, targeted for Q2.

guidance_outlook: Consolidated sales growth: FY27 guidance of about 4-4.5% reported, or 11-12% excluding Foskor and Awuko; management says it could reach about 15% on a comparable basis given the order book.
Consolidated Abrasives sales growth: guidance of 5.5-6% retained; 11-12% excluding Awuko (about INR 108 crores).
Consolidated Ceramics sales growth: raised to 23-25% from 15-15.5%; management expects the Ceramics margin to be at the higher end of the guidance.
Consolidated Electrominerals sales: guidance of a 6.5-7% decline retained (reported basis); 8-9% growth excluding Foskor, and management says this could be 9-10%.

Margins: Abrasives 9.5-10% and Electrominerals 9-9.5% retained, with Ceramics 20.5-21% maintained. Q1 consolidated Abrasives margin was about 2.5% excluding the Sterling gain, which management attributes to Awuko losses.
Capex of about INR 400 crores for FY27 retained. Rhodius guidance of about 5% growth with a small PAT loss is unchanged.
capex_capacity: Consolidated capex was INR 53 crores in Q1 FY27 against INR 64 crores a year earlier; the FY27 target of about INR 400 crores is unchanged, and management would not give project-wise splits.

FY27 capex covers expansion in advanced ceramics for power electronics (including substrates), metallized tubes, rings and brazed assemblies, brown-fused alumina expansion, an integrated furnace for thermal spray powders and a zirconia furnace.
Metallized substrate facility is being set up with one anchor customer and a technology tie-up; it should be commissioned in FY27, with revenue from FY28.

Semiconductor wafer fab equipment components: small in FY27, picking up in FY28, with a peak targeted for FY30. Aerospace and defence will improve in FY27 with the main ramp from FY28. Powder purity is moving from 5N to 6N.
Refractories capacity expansion is on track, per management.
demand_pricing: Standalone Abrasives growth was volume-driven with very small price increases; management sees early easing of Chinese import competition but says exchange rates and China's export-rebate changes make the trend unclear.
Ceramics: growth was seen across segments; Wear Ceramics returned to growth this quarter after several quarters, and Metallized Cylinders and Engineered Ceramics are growing mainly through exports.

Electrominerals: volume-led, with treated-product mix helping margins; little or no price increase. Export share is rising toward 40%, helped by European duties on Chinese imports, with US and Asia efforts under way.

Abrasives cost push: oil-linked inputs such as resins rose sharply in May and June, with oil reaching about $117 a barrel. Grains (80-85% of COGS) rose only 3-5%. The US-Iran conflict that began end-February 2026 drove the cost pressure.
Management said it will not pass on further price increases until the cost environment is clearer, and will decide one quarter at a time.

qa_highlights.question: Ravi (Avendus): How much of standalone Abrasives growth is value vs volume, traction by sub-segment, and are Chinese import changes helping share gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth was predominantly volume-driven with very small price increases. Import competition from China has just started to ease, but management said exchange rates and China's export-benefit withdrawal make the trend unclear; it sees the trend as positive.

qa_highlights.question: Ravi: Where is Ceramics traction strongest across Wear, Technical, Metallized Cylinders and Engineered Ceramics, and is Metallized Cylinder/Engineered Ceramics growth domestic or export?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth optimism is across all segments except Wear, which is normal growth; Wear returned to growth this quarter after several quarters. Metallized Cylinder and Engineered Ceramics growth is predominantly export.

qa_highlights.question: Harshit (Equirus): How will semiconductor wafer fab, aerospace/defence and substrate revenues phase across FY27 and FY28, and does the Ceramics guidance upgrade come mainly from SOFC?
qa_highlights.answer: Substrate facility to be set up in FY27 with revenue from FY28; wafer fab components very small in FY27, picking up in FY28 and peaking in FY30; aerospace/defence slightly better in FY27 with main ramp from FY28. The upgrade is a combination of Engineered Ceramics, Metallized Cylinders and SOFC Ceramics, with no split given.

qa_highlights.question: Harshit: What are plans for zirconia products and Foskor divestment progress, and what drove the Electrominerals volume vs price split?
qa_highlights.answer: Management has a couple of options after discussions with South African partners and aims to close the Foskor process by Q2; a fuller update is promised then. Electrominerals growth was mostly volume and product mix (treated products), with very little or no price increase.

qa_highlights.question: Harshit: Why was Abrasives margin under pressure if Electrominerals prices were not up significantly?
qa_highlights.answer: Grains (80-85% of COGS) rose only 3-5% and were offset by normal price increases; the pressure came from oil-linked inputs such as resins, which rose sharply in May and June with oil reaching about $117 a barrel, plus fuel costs.

qa_highlights.question: Amit Anwani (PL Capital): What is the strategic view on VAW Russia, its utilisation and sales update, and SOFC contribution and volume vs price in the 11-12% comparable guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: No change in Russian business, which remains domestic-focused; management's aim is to stay put, comply with laws and serve the domestic market. Full-year growth is expected to be predominantly volume-driven with normal price increases; no individual SOFC split was shared, and pricing beyond normal will be decided one quarter at a time.

qa_highlights.question: Varun Jain (Dolat): Excluding the Sterling gain, consolidated Abrasives margin is about 2.5% versus 9-10% guidance; what is the comment, and what is the CAPEX breakdown and unallocated expense run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the gap is largely Awuko losses, which are still being incurred, so it holds the 9-10% guidance. Project-wise CAPEX split was not shared. Consolidated unallocable expense of INR 19 crores was mainly a forex loss versus a gain last year.

qa_highlights.question: Sajal Kapoor (Antifragile): How does the group distinguish a temporary setback from a signal to exit, and how does it make decisions in semiconductors and defence without operating history?
qa_highlights.answer: Awuko and Foskor were exited after management gave enough time; it waits at least four to eight quarters before deciding if a trend is temporary. For semicon, it is entering as a supplier of ceramics to fab equipment makers, building on 40-50 years of ceramics experience and working via anchor customers.

qa_highlights.question: Aditya (Kotak): How large are exports in standalone Electrominerals, and is European duty on Chinese imports a driver; what is the semicon 6N and substrate roadmap and any inorganic plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Export share has risen from about 20% earlier to 35% last year and is now on a path to 40%. Europe's duties are helping, with US and Asia efforts under way. 5N to 6N powder purity is being worked on; substrate benefits start FY28. Management said the focus is to remain a raw material supplier, with no inorganic plans stated.

risks_watch: Abrasives margin recovery: standalone Abrasives margin fell to 10.4% from 13.1% YoY; oil-linked resin and fuel cost push (about INR 16 crores) and whether normal price increases can offset it, given no further pricing is planned until the cost environment clears.
Awuko winding-up completion (guided within about a quarter) and the exceptional costs still to come; Q1 Abrasives losses from Awuko depress consolidated margins.
Foskor divestment or exit: options being explored, targeted to close by Q2; Q1 consolidated PBIT absorbed about INR 17 crores of Foskor loss.

Consolidated Ceramics margin: management expects the high end of 20.5-21% guidance, but standalone Ceramics PBIT was flat YoY on fuel, alumina and unabsorbed costs in new semicon and aerospace/defence lines.
Sustainability of Electrominerals export-led growth (33% standalone YoY) given that pricing was flat and the growth was mostly volume and mix.
VAW Russia: RUB sales down 14.1% YoY with geopolitical uncertainty; management says it is too difficult to predict and the aim is to stay put.
Unallocable costs: consolidated INR 19 crores in Q1 due to forex loss and lower interest income; forex swings may recur.
key_quotes: Growth at standalone level was broad-based and driven by all three segments.
So, it's going to be very tough and it's going to be tough for us to say that based on which we will start putting up price, etc., is also going to be tough.
We always wait at least four to eight quarters to see whether these are temporary trends or fundamentally things are changing.
Right now our focus is that we should be a raw material supplier and so we stay focused on that.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on growth and the raised Ceramics guidance, but cautious and at times evasive on pricing, the cost outlook and project-level details. It repeatedly said the situation changes daily and that it will decide one quarter at a time, and declined to give CAPEX project splits or a SOFC breakdown.
